OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Improve the bound Var(log Z_n) = O(n/log n) for directed polymers in random environment in general dimension to a power improvement n^{1-eps}. Source: Chatterjee: Chaos, concentration and multiple valleys, 2008, with open questions, Section 12, problem (3), p. 59. Status notes: In d = 1+1 with exactly solvable weights (log-gamma, exponential last-passage) the exponent 2/3 (variance n^{2/3}) is a theorem; for general weights in any dimension the BKS-type n/log n remains the best general bound to this session's knowledge; cf. the FPP variance problem in the Codex campaign (P-a/ chi = 1/3 target).
Posed in Chatterjee: Chaos, concentration and multiple valleys, 2008, with open questions

record.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Same block as the first-passage percolation sublinear variance problem; record the exact reduction. Result: The n/log n bound is the BKS entropy method; a power improvement n^{1-eps} would follow from a chaos exponent: if the polymer measure decorrelates under a noise of size n^{-eps'} on the environment (superconcentration with a rate), Talagrand's/Chatterjee's equivalence gives Var(log Z_n) <= n^{1-eps}. Conversely, the variance exponent is tied to the transversal fluctuation exponent by the KPZ scaling relation chi = 2 xi - 1 (Chatterjee 2013 proved the relation rigorously for FPP under existence of the exponents), so a power improvement needs a quantitative transversal-fluctuation bound xi < 1 with an explicit gap, which is known only in the exactly solvable models. The obstruction is the same wall the campaign records for FPP; no new input. Obstruction: Quantitative chaos rate or transversal fluctuation bound unavailable outside integrable models.

record.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check which steps of the d = 2 proof are dimension-dependent. Result: The source's d = 1+1 proof establishes superconcentration of the free energy (variance o(n)) via hypercontractivity and then chaos from superconcentration through the general equivalence theorem; the dimension-dependent step is the variance bound Var(log Z_n) = O(n/log n), obtained from the Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm influence inequality applied to the free energy with the influence of a single site bounded by the expected overlap of two polymers at that site, whose sum over sites is the expected overlap, of order n in the strong disorder regime. The BKS argument is dimension-free provided the polymer is in the strong disorder phase (positive overlap); in d >= 3 the strong disorder phase exists at low temperature (Comets-Yoshida), so the variance bound O(n/log n) transfers and superconcentration follows; the equivalence theorem then gives chaos at the level of the overlap between the polymers at slightly perturbed environments. So the obstruction the source mentions ('certain parts do not work in higher dimensions') must be in the identification that the overlap in the strong-disorder phase is of order n (needed for the influence sum to be order n and the BKS gain to be meaningful): in d >= 3 at low temperature the overlap is positive but the known lower bounds are only qualitative (positive limit of the overlap along the endpoint), not quantitative along the whole path. Rigorous partial: superconcentration (Var log Z_n = o(n)) in d >= 3 at low temperature follows from BKS if the expected path overlap is of order n, which is a consequence of the strong disorder characterisation via the endpoint overlap only if the overlap is positive at a positive fraction of times; this last step is plausible but I found no reference proving it in d >= 3. Reduction recorded. Obstruction: Quantitative (order n) path overlap in the strong disorder phase for d >= 3.
